documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Prenatal update for primary care, visit of 03/24/2025.

29-year-old G1 at 28 weeks 2 days. Feeling well, good fetal movement. Growth appropriate for dates; anatomy survey in January was normal. Glucose challenge normal. Tdap given today. No HSV prodrome or lesions this pregnancy; continuing valacyclovir 500 mg daily and prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Next visits every two weeks from 32 weeks. She knows to call at once for any genital lesion, tingling or labor.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Operative Note: Cesarean Delivery
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OPERATIVE NOTE
Date: 06/11/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: intrauterine pregnancy at 39 weeks 4 days in active labor; active genital herpes lesions.
Postoperative diagnosis: same; delivered.
Procedure: emergent primary low transverse cesarean delivery.
Anesthesia: spinal.

Indication: 29-year-old G1 with genital HSV-2 on daily valacyclovir suppression, admitted in active labor with regular contractions and cervical change. She had no fever, urinary burning or abnormal discharge. On exam there were several clustered vesicles on a red base over the labia and perineum. With active lesions in labor, vaginal birth would expose the baby to HSV, so we proceeded with cesarean.

Findings: viable male infant from vertex position, Apgars 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Normal uterus, tubes and ovaries. Clear fluid.

Uncomplicated procedure. Pfannenstiel skin incision closed subcuticularly. Mother and infant to recovery in stable condition.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/11/2025, discharged 06/14/2025

Diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered by emergent primary low transverse cesarean for active genital HSV lesions in labor. Genital HSV-2 on suppression. Past history of acute hepatitis E (2024, resolved) and giardiasis (2023, treated).

Course: delivered a healthy boy on 6/11 (Apgars 8 and 9). No rash, breathing trouble or enlarged liver or spleen on newborn exam; pediatrics is following him for the HSV exposure per protocol. Her recovery was routine: afebrile, incision clean, pain controlled with oral medicines, ambulating, voiding, tolerating a diet. Valacyclovir continued throughout.

Discharge medications:
- valacyclovir 500 mg by mouth daily
- prenatal vitamin daily
- ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed, about 2 weeks
- acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed, about 2 weeks
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: incision check at 2 weeks, postpartum visit at 6 weeks. Call for fever, heavy bleeding, incision redness or drainage, or low mood.

documents.title: Postpartum Check-in Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after receiving delivery records. Home since Saturday with her son. Incision sore but improving, using ibuprofen a few times a day. No fever, bleeding tapering. Baby feeding and seen by pediatrics yesterday, she says he is doing fine. Sleep is in pieces but mood okay, has help at home. OB incision check next week. Reminded to keep taking valacyclovir and to call with any concerns.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit Letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit, 07/23/2025, six weeks after cesarean.

Recovering well. Incision healed. Bleeding has stopped. Postpartum depression screen negative. Pelvic exam normal, no lesions. Cleared for exercise and usual activity. Continuing valacyclovir 500 mg daily. Cervical screening due this fall with primary care.

We will see her as needed. Thank you.
Obstetrics

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Just turned 30. Son is 4 months old and thriving. Back to her dissertation part time. Recovered well from the cesarean in June; OB postpartum visit in July was normal. Stopped the prenatal vitamin in September on her own. No HSV outbreaks since the one in labor. Sleep broken but manageable; mood good, partner and family helping.

Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg daily. NKDA.
PSH: low transverse cesarean 6/2025.
Social: no tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, Pfannenstiel scar well healed. Pelvic: external genitalia normal without lesions; cervix normal, Pap with HPV collected. Skin clear. PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
- Genital HSV-2: continue suppression.
- Status post cesarean, recovered.
- Health maintenance: Pap with HPV co-test today (age 30). CBC after pregnancy and TSH given her mother's thyroid history. Flu and COVID today. Prenatal vitamin off the list.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 06/08/2026 18:25 by EMS

CC: confusion.

HPI: 30-year-old woman with genital HSV-2 on valacyclovir, whose last outbreak was at delivery in 2025 and led to a cesarean. Per her roommate, she had a headache, felt dizzy and nauseated from the morning on and said she would sleep it off. Later the roommate found her drowsy and muddled on the couch beside an unvented gas space heater that had been running in the apartment. Roommate reports no drugs or alcohol and no fall or injury.

PMH: genital HSV-2; giardiasis 2023, treated; acute hepatitis E 2024, resolved. PSH: cesarean 2025.
Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: P 110, RR 20, BP 122/70, T 37.1. Confused, speech mildly slurred. Skin flushed bright red. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Clumsy rapid alternating movements bilaterally; strength full and symmetric, no focal deficit.

Course: 100% oxygen by nonrebreather started on arrival. Pulse oximeter then read 96%, which is not reassuring here: a standard probe reads carboxyhemoglobin as oxyhemoglobin. Arterial blood gas with co-oximetry: carboxyhemoglobin 26%, pH 7.36, PaCO2 35, PaO2 412 on nonrebreather, bicarbonate 20. Lactate 2.6. hs-troponin I 4. Urine hCG negative. CBC normal; BMP normal except bicarbonate 21. Monitor and 12-lead ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic changes.

Impression: carbon monoxide poisoning from an unvented gas heater, with confusion and cerebellar signs; airway intact.
Disposition: discussed with hyperbaric medicine; transferred on 100% oxygen to the regional hyperbaric unit. Fire department notified to check the apartment.

documents.title: Hyperbaric Medicine Discharge Summary
documents.author: hyperbaric medicine
documents.body:
HYPERBARIC MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/08/2026, discharged 06/09/2026

Diagnosis: acute carbon monoxide poisoning (carboxyhemoglobin 26% at the sending ED) with confusion, slurred speech and impaired rapid alternating movements.

Course: arrived on 100% oxygen. Three hyperbaric oxygen sessions within 24 hours, the first started on arrival. Carboxyhemoglobin 2% after the first session. Tolerated all sessions; ears equalized without difficulty. By the next morning she was fully oriented, speech normal, rapid alternating movements normal, gait steady. No chest pain.

Discharge: home 06/09. Valacyclovir 500 mg daily, unchanged. NKDA.
Instructions: no gas heater use until the appliance is inspected or removed; working CO detectors on every level. Delayed neurologic symptoms can appear in the weeks after CO poisoning; call for trouble with memory, concentration, mood, movement or new headaches. PCP follow-up within one week.
